questions: Did s-bend and slalom max_error fall below 0.06 m with the 60 mm span? By how much on each track?
Did oval progress hold at 0.65 or more with finish count near 20 of 20? If it fell, did it fall because of steering oscillation or because the robot was too slow?
What kp, ki, kd and base_speed did you use at the 60 mm span on the 0.10 m track, and did you scale kp for the wider span?
Do line_loss_events stay near 1 or fewer per run on the s-bend and slalom with the 15 mm pitch?
Do the remaining bend excursions start before or after a line-loss event, and do they cluster at one bend sharpness?

intent: Keep wheel_track 0.10 m, which held oval progress at 0.995 and slightly reduced slalom max_error, and widen the sensor span from 50 mm to 60 mm (15 mm pitch, 12 mm footprints, y 0.05). The aim is to test whether a wider array reduces the bend excursions that have stayed on the 0.06 m plateau. Expected: s-bend and slalom max_error fall below 0.06 m, oval progress stays at or above 0.65, and line losses stay near 1 per run. If oval progress falls below about 0.65 or steering oscillation rises above about 0.35, the Integrator should lower kp first. If that does not restore progress, revert to the 50 mm span with wheel_track 0.10, which is the current best.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that wheel_track 0.10 keeps the oval finishing (progress 0.995) but does not lower s-bend max_error (0.0676 m) and only slightly lowers slalom (0.0608 m). Turn rate is therefore not the main limit on bend excursions. The span test at 60 mm checks whether a wider array can see the tape far enough out to keep the robot inside 0.06 m on bends. Iteration 3 showed a progress collapse at 60 mm under a weaker controller, so the result here is decisive for whether 60 mm stays in the design. If the excursions persist at 60 mm, the next test is a lead change (y 0.04) or a longer lead on the bend tracks only, not further span changes.
rationale: Iteration 7 (wheel_track 0.10 m, 50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05) scored 399.7, the best so far. Oval progress is 0.995 with 20 of 20 finishes and oval max_error 0.032 m, so the oval is solved and the 0.65 floor holds with a wide margin. The wheel_track change did not move the s-bend and slalom excursions below the off-track line. s-bend max_error went from 0.0682 to 0.0676 m, essentially unchanged. Slalom max_error improved from 0.0645 to 0.0608 m, close to 0.06 m but not under it. Neither track finished. s-bend steering oscillation rose to 0.317, which is above the 0.3 threshold, but this is a steering-gain signal on a track where oval progress still holds, so it is a tuning matter for the Integrator and not a reason to revert geometry. Across iterations 0 to 7, max_error on the bend tracks has stayed on a 0.059 to 0.068 m plateau under every span, footprint, lead, wheel_track and controller change. Line losses on the development tracks are about 1 per run, so the tape is not being lost. The agreed rule applies: s-bend and slalom max_error still at or above 0.06 m while oval progress holds means the next geometry test is a sensor span change from 50 mm to 60 mm. I keep wheel_track at 0.10 m, which the oval result supports, and move to 60 mm span (x = -0.03, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.03) with 12 mm footprints at y 0.05. The main risk is that iteration 3 (60 mm, 12 mm, wheel 0.12, weaker controller) fell to oval progress 0.275. The current controller has a much larger oval margin, so I judge that result worth testing, but the Integrator should be ready to lower kp or fall back to 50 mm if oval progress drops below about 0.65. Body, wheel radius and mass stay fixed so that the span is the only geometry variable.
